mainTopic: Things that help or harm Torah learning, honor for the leaders of the סנהדרין, and the story behind the labels 'אחרים' and 'יש אומרים'
overview: The amud opens by finishing a point about how destructive mice are. A ברייתא then lists five things that make a person forget his learning and five things that bring it back. Two items are supported by sayings of רבי יוחנן (olive oil) and רבא (wine and spices). The salt item leads to a dispute about one or two fingers. A list of ten things harmful to learning follows. Next, a ברייתא describes the honor shown to the נשיא, the אב בית דין and the חכם, and how scholars and their sons are seated. רב פפא, רבא and רב add limits to some of these rules. Finally, רבי יוחנן tells the story behind the honor rules: רבי מאיר and רבי נתן tried to embarrass and replace רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, failed, and were punished by having their teachings quoted as 'אחרים' and 'יש אומרים'. The amud ends with רבי teaching his son a teaching of 'אחרים', and that exchange continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Mice gnaw even on a hoe handle
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that mice gnaw even on the wooden handle of a hoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They gnaw even on the handle of a hoe.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds one more example to the earlier discussion of how mice damage things: they chew even on a hoe's handle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wooden handle is not food, so chewing it shows the mouse damages things for no benefit. This line closes the discussion about mice just before the ברייתא about forgetting learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Handle (the wooden shaft of a tool)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
They gnaw even on the handle of a hoe.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the mice from just before. The ד in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שׁוּפְתָּא דְּמָרָא גָּיְיצִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous page about the mouse's destructive nature.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mice gnaw even on non-food items like a hoe handle.

steps.title: Five things that make a person forget his learning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists things that cause a person to forget his תלמוד, plus an extra item from יש אומרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Five things make a person forget his learning: eating from what a mouse or a cat ate, eating an animal's heart, regularly eating olives, drinking leftover washing water, and washing one foot on top of the other. Some say: also one who puts his clothes under his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists habits which cause a person to forget what he learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, connected to the mouse and cat discussion just before. The list is mostly about food and washing habits. The יש אומרים opinion adds one more item: sleeping with your clothes under your head.

keyTerms.meaning: The place under his head (where a pillow goes)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Five things make one forget his learning:
One who eats from what a mouse ate
and from what a cat ate,
and one who eats the heart of an animal,
and one who regularly eats olives,
and one who drinks water left over from washing,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָרוֹחֵץ רַגְלָיו זוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי זוֹ.
phrases.english: and one who washes his feet, one on top of the other.
And some say:
Also one who puts his clothes under his head.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן. חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים מְשַׁכְּחִים אֶת הַתַּלְמוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, connected to the mouse discussion through the first item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Certain eating and washing habits cause a person to forget his learning.

steps.title: Five things that bring back forgotten learning
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא lists the opposite: things that restore learning, plus an extra item from יש אומרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five things bring back learning: bread baked on coals, and even more so the coals themselves; eating a hard-boiled egg without salt; regularly using olive oil; regularly using wine and spices; and drinking water left over from kneading dough. Some say: also one who dips his finger in salt and eats it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a matching list of things that help a person remember his learning again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list is built as the opposite of the first list. Notice the pairs: olives make you forget, but olive oil brings learning back. Leftover washing water hurts, but leftover dough water helps.
steps.whatToRemember: Two opposite lists: five things make you forget your learning, and five things bring it back. The second list often mirrors the first, like olives versus olive oil.

phrases.english: Five things bring back learning:
Bread baked on coals
and all the more so the coals themselves,
phrases.notes: This means warming yourself by the heat of the coals. Nobody is eating coals.

phrases.english: and one who eats a hard-boiled egg without salt,
and one who regularly uses olive oil,
and one who regularly uses wine and spices,
and one who drinks water left over from kneading dough.
And some say:
Also one who dips his finger in salt and eats it.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים מְשִׁיבִים אֶת הַתַּלְמוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same ברייתא, giving the opposite list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Certain foods and habits restore forgotten learning.

steps.title: Olive oil item supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's olive oil line supports רבי יוחנן's teaching that olives make you forget and olive oil brings learning back.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who regularly uses olive oil' supports רבי יוחנן, who said: Just as the olive makes a person forget seventy years of learning, olive oil brings back seventy years of learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that one line of the ברייתא backs up a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that olives and olive oil have opposite effects. The ברייתא lists olives in the 'forget' list and olive oil in the 'bring back' list, so it matches his view exactly.

phrases.english: 'One who regularly uses olive oil.'
This supports Rabbi Yochanan,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַזַּיִת מְשַׁכֵּחַ תַּלְמוּד שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: Just as the olive makes one forget seventy years of learning,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ שֶׁמֶן זַיִת מֵשִׁיב תַּלְמוּד שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: so olive oil brings back seventy years of learning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks out one item from the ברייתא and links it to an אמורא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's statement that olives cause forgetting and olive oil restores learning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's listing of olives under 'forget' and olive oil under 'bring back.'

steps.title: Wine and spices item supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's wine and spices line supports רבא's statement that wine and fragrances made him wise.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who regularly uses wine and spices' supports רבא, who said: Wine and fragrances made me wise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that another line of the ברייתא backs up a statement of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said from his own experience that wine and spices sharpened his mind. The ברייתא says the same thing when it lists them as restoring learning.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא backs up two of the ברייתא's 'bring back' items with sayings of אמוראים: olive oil (רבי יוחנן) and wine and spices (רבא).

phrases.english: 'And one who regularly uses wine and spices.'
This supports Rava,
as Rava said:
Wine and fragrances made me wise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 4, applied to the next item in the list.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's statement that wine and fragrances made him wise.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's listing of wine and spices among things that restore learning.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Dipping only one finger in salt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line about dipping a finger in salt, and ריש לקיש adds that this means one finger.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said that dipping your finger in salt and eating it brings back learning. ריש לקיש said: that is with one finger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to one item on the ברייתא's list of things that restore learning. ריש לקיש explains how many fingers it refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said 'his finger' without a number. ריש לקיש makes it specific: one finger. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא shows that תנאים argued about exactly this.

phrases.english: "And one who dips his finger in salt"
Reish Lakish said: And that is with one finger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: וּבְאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to one item in the 'restoring learning' list and explains it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The salt practice works when you dip one finger.

steps.title: The same question is a dispute between תנאים, with a memory aid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that ריש לקיש's view matches רבי יהודה, who argues with רבי יוסי about one finger or two, and it gives a memory aid: קמיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים. רבי יהודה says: one finger, not two. רבי יוסי says: two fingers, not three. Your memory aid is קמיצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that ריש לקיש's 'one finger' is really one side of an older argument between תנאים. Then it gives a trick for remembering the numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יהודה (one finger). רבי יוסי allows two fingers but not three. The memory aid קמיצה helps you remember the argument is about 'one or two': when the ring finger is bent down, one finger stands on one side and two on the other.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between tanna'im:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַחַת וְלֹא שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: One finger, but not two.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שְׁתַּיִם וְלֹא שָׁלֹשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: Two fingers, but not three.
And your memory aid: the ring finger.
phrases.notes: Bend the ring finger down and you see one finger on one side and two on the other, so you remember 'one or two.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַנָּאֵי, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַחַת וְלֹא שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places ריש לקיש's statement inside an older argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's statement that the salt practice uses one finger
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's view: one finger and not two

steps.title: Ten things that are harmful for Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: A list of ten things that make learning difficult, plus an extra item from יש אומרים: reading the writing on a grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ten things are bad for learning: passing under a camel's bit (and even more so under the camel itself), passing between two camels, a man passing between two women, a woman passing between two men, passing under the bad smell of a carcass, passing under a bridge with no water under it for forty days, eating bread that is not fully baked, eating meat from a זוהמא ליסטרון, drinking from a water channel that runs through a cemetery, and looking at the face of a dead person. Some say: also reading the writing on a grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another list, this time of ten things that are 'hard' for learning. It continues the theme of what helps and what harms one's memory of Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new list, like the earlier lists of things that cause forgetting (step 2). Passing under the camel itself is not a separate item; it is a 'how much more so' add-on to the first item, so the count still comes to ten. The יש אומרים opinion adds an eleventh item.

keyTerms.meaning: A bit or halter (the camel's head strap)
A kitchen tool used to skim soup

steps.confusionAlert: Don't count 'under the camel itself' as its own item. It is a 'how much more so' add-on to the first item, which is how the list comes to exactly ten.
steps.whatToRemember: There are ten things harmful for learning. Many involve passing through or near certain places, eating improperly prepared food, or contact with death.

phrases.english: Ten things are harmful for learning:
One who passes under the bit of the camel,
and all the more so under the camel itself;
and one who passes between two camels;
and one who passes between two women;
and a woman who passes between two men;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָעוֹבֵר מִתַּחַת רֵיחַ רַע שֶׁל נְבֵילָה,
phrases.english: and one who passes under the bad smell of a carcass;
and one who passes under a bridge

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא עָבְרוּ תַּחְתָּיו מַיִם אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם,
phrases.english: that water has not passed under for forty days;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאוֹכֵל פַּת שֶׁלֹּא בָּשַׁל כׇּל צָרְכּוֹ,
phrases.english: and one who eats bread that was not fully baked;
and one who eats meat from a zuhama listeron;
phrases.notes: This is a kitchen tool, a spoon on one end and a fork on the other, used to skim the film off soup.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשּׁוֹתֶה מֵאַמַּת הַמַּיִם הָעוֹבֶרֶת בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת,
phrases.english: and one who drinks from a water channel that runs through a cemetery;
and one who looks at the face of a dead person.
And some say: also one who reads the writing
that is on a grave.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים קָשִׁים לַתַּלְמוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new list of harmful things to the earlier lists about forgetting and remembering learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten listed actions are harmful for learning; some add reading the writing on a grave.

steps.title: How people honor the נשיא, the אב בית דין, and the חכם when they enter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes three levels of honor: everyone stands for the נשיא, two rows form for the אב בית דין, and people stand one by one for the חכם as he passes.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the נשיא enters, everyone stands and does not sit until he tells them to sit. When the אב בית דין enters, people form a row on each side for him until he sits in his place. When the חכם enters, one person stands and another sits as he passes, until he sits in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about the honor given to the three top leaders of the סנהדרין when they enter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honor goes down step by step with rank. For the נשיא everyone stands and waits for permission to sit. For the אב בית דין two rows stand until he is seated. For the חכם only the people near him stand as he walks by.

keyTerms.meaning: The third-ranking member of the סנהדרין

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that honor for Torah leaders follows their rank, a theme that fits מסכת הוריות's discussion of who takes precedence.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
When the Nasi enters, all the people stand,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין יוֹשְׁבִים עַד שֶׁאוֹמֵר לָהֶם: שֵׁבוּ.
phrases.english: and they do not sit until he says to them: Sit.
When the Av Beit Din enters,

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשִׂים לוֹ שׁוּרָה אַחַת מִכָּאן וְשׁוּרָה אַחַת מִכָּאן,
phrases.english: they form for him one row on this side and one row on that side,
until he sits in his place.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁחָכָם נִכְנָס, אֶחָד עוֹמֵד וְאֶחָד יוֹשֵׁב,
phrases.english: When the Chakham enters, one stands and one sits,
phrases.notes: As he walks by, the people near him stand, and the ones he has already passed sit back down.

phrases.english: until he sits in his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֶׁהַנָּשִׂיא נִכְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the honor shown to Torah leaders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honor on entering goes by rank: everyone stands for the נשיא, two rows form for the אב בית דין, and people near the חכם stand as he passes.

steps.title: Scholars needed by the public may step over the crowd
steps.stepSummary: Sons of חכמים and תלמידי חכמים whom the public needs may step over the seated people, and one who stepped out for a need may come back to his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sons of חכמים and תלמידי חכמים, when the public needs them, may step over the heads of the people. If one went out for a need, he may come back in and sit in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues, allowing certain scholars to step over the crowd to reach their seats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally stepping over seated people is disrespectful to them. Here it is allowed because the public depends on these scholars. A scholar who left to relieve himself may also return to his seat, even though he must pass through the crowd again.

keyTerms.meaning: Step over the heads of the people
Went out for a need (to relieve himself)

phrases.english: Sons of Sages and Torah scholars,
at a time when the public needs them,
may step over the heads of the people.
If he went out for a need,
phrases.notes: He means going out to relieve himself.

phrases.english: he may come back in and sit in his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי חֲכָמִים וְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁרַבִּים צְרִיכִים לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a rule about scholars reaching their seats.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scholars the public needs may step over the crowd, and one who left for a need may return to his seat.

steps.title: Where the sons of a community leader sit
steps.stepSummary: Sons of scholars whose father is a community leader sit in front of their father: facing him if they can follow the learning, and facing the people if they cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sons of תלמידי חכמים whose father is appointed a leader over the community: if they are able to understand and listen, they come in and sit in front of their father with their backs to the people. If they are not able to understand and listen, they come in and sit in front of their father with their faces toward the people.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the seating of a leader's sons. Either way they sit in front of their father, but which way they face depends on whether they can follow the learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sons who can learn face their father like students. Sons who cannot follow still get a seat of honor, but they face the people. This way everyone sees they sit there out of respect for their father, not as students.

keyTerms.meaning: A leader appointed over the community
The understanding to listen and learn

phrases.english: Sons of Torah scholars
whose father is appointed leader over the community,
when they have the understanding to listen,
they come in and sit before their father
with their backs toward the people.
When they do not have the understanding to listen,
they come in and sit before their father
with their faces toward the people.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁמְּמוּנִּים אֲבִיהֶם פַּרְנָס עַל הַצִּבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא, moving from the scholars themselves to their sons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leader's sons sit in front of him: facing him if they can learn, facing the people if they cannot.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק: The sons are honored at a feast too
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק adds that even at a feast, these sons are seated right next to their fathers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק says: even at a feast, they are made 'attachments' and seated next to their fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא adds to the ברייתא: the honor given to a leader's sons applies at a feast as well, not only in the study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ברייתא spoke about seating where learning takes place. רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק extends the honor to a social setting: at a feast too, the sons sit attached to their fathers.

keyTerms.meaning: A feast, such as a wedding party
Attachments: seated right beside their fathers

steps.whatToRemember: Honor is given to Torah leaders according to rank, and some of that honor carries over to their sons, both in the study hall and at a feast.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:
Even at a feast
they make them attachments.
phrases.notes: He means they are seated right next to their fathers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר: אַף בְּבֵית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the honor of the leader's sons from the study hall to a feast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At a feast, too, a leader's sons are seated next to their fathers.

steps.title: Returning to your seat only applies to a short bathroom trip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule that one who stepped out may return to his seat. רב פפא limits it to small needs, because a person should have taken care of big needs beforehand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'If he went out for a need, he comes back and sits in his place.' רב פפא said: This was said only for small needs. For big needs, no, because he should have checked himself beforehand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from step 10, and רב פפא narrows it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stepping over seated people to get back to your place bothers them. רב פפא says that is allowed only when the need could not be planned, like urinating. A long trip for defecating could have been handled before the lesson, so the person must take the blame and not bother others.

keyTerms.meaning: For a need (here, to use the bathroom)
To check himself, to take care of his needs ahead of time

phrases.english: The Master said: If he went out for a need —
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets belong to the corrected wording. This quotes the ברייתא from step 10, and 'need' means the bathroom.

phrases.english: he comes in and sits in his place.
Rav Pappa said:
They only said this for small [needs],
but for big [needs] — no,
he should have checked himself from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר מר יצא לצורך נכנס ויושב במקומו אמר רב פפא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the rule in step 10 and narrows it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar may return to his seat only after stepping out for small needs, not big needs.

steps.title: Support: a person should train himself to go morning and evening
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, teaches that a person should get used to relieving himself early and late in the day. This supports רב פפא's claim that the person should have planned ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should always train himself to relieve himself in the early morning and in the evening, so that he will not have to go far away during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רב to back up רב פפא's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's advice shows that big needs can be scheduled. So someone who leaves in the middle of the lesson for big needs did not plan well, which explains why he loses his seat.

keyTerms.meaning: Always, a word that introduces good advice for life
Early in the morning and in the evening
Go far away (to find a private place)

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
A person should always train himself
[to relieve himself] early in the morning and in the evening,
so that he will not have to go far away.

steps.triggerLanguage: דאמר רב יהודה אמר רב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reason רב פפא gave in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's reason that one should have checked himself beforehand
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's teaching that a person should train himself to relieve himself morning and evening

steps.title: Nowadays people are weaker, so even after big needs one may return
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that today, since people's health is weaker, a person may return to his seat even after leaving for big needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Nowadays, when the world is weak, one may return even after big needs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא updates רב פפא's limit for his own time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's limit assumed that people can control when they need to go. רבא says people today are weaker and cannot always plan this, so leaving is no longer counted as his fault, and he may come back to his seat.

keyTerms.meaning: The world (people's health) has become weak

steps.whatToRemember: In general a scholar who stepped out may return to his seat. רב פפא limited this to small needs, but רבא says that nowadays it covers big needs too.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Nowadays, when the world is weak —
even for big [needs] too [he may return].

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא האידנא דחלשא עלמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רב פפא's limit because times have changed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nowadays one may return to his seat even after leaving for big needs.

steps.title: Sons sit beside their fathers at a feast only while the father is alive and present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק's rule about seating sons next to fathers at a feast, and רבא limits it to when the father is alive and there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק says: Even at a feast they seat them right beside their fathers. רבא said: This is while their father is alive and in their father's presence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the line from step 12, and רבא adds a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The special seat is given because of the father's honor, not the son's own standing. So it only applies while the father is alive and actually at the feast.

keyTerms.meaning: Attachments: people seated right next to someone

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
Even at a feast
they make them attachments.
phrases.notes: He means the sons are seated right next to their fathers, as in step 12.

phrases.english: Rava said:
During their fathers' lifetime, in their fathers' presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק אומר אף בבית המשתה עושים אותם סניפים אמר רבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 12 and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sons are seated beside their fathers at a feast only while the father is alive and present.

steps.title: The ברייתא of honors was taught in the days of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that the ברייתא about levels of honor was made in the time of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and he names who held each position.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This teaching was made in the days of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was the נשיא, רבי מאיר was the חכם, and רבי נתן was the אב בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts telling the story behind the ברייתא in step 9. This step sets the scene by naming the three leaders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three positions in the ברייתא matched a real person at that time. This helps us see why a rule separating them was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Was taught (was made into a teaching)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
In the days of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
this teaching was taught.
phrases.notes: 'This teaching' is the ברייתא about standing for the נשיא, the אב בית דין and the חכם from step 9.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel was the Nasi,
Rabbi Meir was the Ḥakham,
Rabbi Natan was the Av Beit Din.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יוחנן בימי רבן שמעון בן גמליאל נישנית משנה זו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the background story of the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא of honors comes from the time of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי מאיר and רבי נתן.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wanted a difference between his honor and theirs
steps.stepSummary: Everyone stood equally for all three leaders. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל felt the נשיא should be honored differently, so he made the ברייתא of honors.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was there, everyone would stand for him. When רבי מאיר and רבי נתן came in, everyone would stand for them too. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: Shouldn't there be a difference between me and them? He set up this ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. We learn why the rule was made: to show a clear difference in honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, everyone stood fully for all three leaders, so there was no sign that the נשיא was higher. The new rule gave each position its own kind of honor, as listed in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: A clear difference, a visible sign

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם,
phrases.english: When Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel was there,
everyone would stand before him.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ עָיְילִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי נָתָן,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Natan would come in,
everyone would stand before them.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
Shouldn't there be a distinction
between mine and theirs?
He set up this teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי הוה רבן שמעון בן גמליאל התם הוו קיימי כולי עלמא מקמיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and explains why the rule was made.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל made the rule of different honors so that the נשיא would be set apart.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי נתן find out about the new rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר and רבי נתן were away the day the rule was made. The next day people did not stand for them as usual, and when they asked why, they were told that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל had made the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: That day רבי מאיר and רבי נתן were not there. The next day, when they came, they saw that people did not stand for them as they usually did. They said: What is this? People told them: This is what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל set up.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. The two Sages notice the change in honor and are told who made it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was made while they were absent, so it took them by surprise. This step prepares the reaction that the story tells next.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא יוֹמָא לָא הֲווֹ רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי נָתָן הָתָם,
phrases.english: That day Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Natan were not there,
the next day, when they came,
they saw that people did not stand before them
as was usually done.
They said: What is this?
People said to them:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי תַּקֵּין רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: This is what Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel set up.

steps.triggerLanguage: ההוא יומא לא הוו רבי מאיר ורבי נתן התם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story by showing how the two Sages learned of the new rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר and רבי נתן learned that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל had reduced the honor shown to them.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's plan to remove the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר suggests to רבי נתן that they test רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on מסכת עוקצין. When he fails, they will use a פסוק to show he is unfit and remove him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said to רבי נתן: I am the חכם and you are the אב בית דין. Let us do to him what he did to us. We will ask him to teach עוקצין, which he does not know. Once it is clear he never learned it, we will quote the פסוק 'Who can express the mighty acts of ה׳, shall make all His praise heard': only someone who can make all His praises heard is fit to speak them. We will remove him, I will become אב בית דין, and you will become נשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. רבי מאיר reacts to losing his honor by planning to test the נשיא in a hard מסכת and remove him from office.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plan has three parts: test him on a rarely learned מסכת, use a פסוק to argue that a leader must know all of Torah, then move each of them up one position. 'כי לדידן' shows this is payback for the new honor rule from Step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sage, the third-ranking position (held by רבי מאיר)
Head of the court, the second-ranking position (held by רבי נתן)
A מסכת in סדר טהרות that is rarely learned
We will remove him from office

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְרַבִּי נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said to Rabbi Natan:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא חָכָם וְאַתְּ אַב בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: I am the Sage, and you are the head of the court,
let us arrange a matter just like he did to us.
phrases.notes: He means: just as the נשיא lowered our honor, let us do something to him.

phrases.english: What shall we do to him?

phrases.aramaic: נֵימָא לֵיהּ: גַּלִּי עוּקְצִים, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Let us say to him: Teach us עוקצים, which he does not know.
And once it is clear that he did not learn it,
we will say to him: "Who can express the mighty acts of ה׳,
shall make all His praise heard,"
meaning: for whom is it fitting to express the mighty acts of ה׳?
For one who is able to make all His praises heard.
We will remove him from office,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵי אֲנָא אַב בֵּית דִּין וְאַתְּ נָשִׂיא.
phrases.english: and I will be head of the court and you will be the Nasi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reaction to finding out about the new honor rule in Step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר plans to embarrass and remove the נשיא by testing him on עוקצים and arguing from a פסוק that a leader must know all of Torah.

steps.title: רבי יעקב בן קדשי quietly warns the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בן קדשי overhears the plan. He worries it will lead to embarrassment, so he sits behind the נשיא's room and recites עוקצין out loud again and again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בן קדשי heard them and said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid, this will lead to embarrassment. He went and sat behind the upper room of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, laid out the מסכת, and recited it and repeated it, recited it and repeated it.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone overhears the plan and finds a quiet way to help the נשיא without openly telling on anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not report the plan. Instead he reviews עוקצין loudly where the נשיא will hear it. This hints to the נשיא that something is coming and also gives him a chance to learn the מסכת.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁמְעִינְהוּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בֶּן קֻדְשַׁי, אֲמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov ben Kudshai heard them and said:
Perhaps, Heaven forbid,
this matter will lead to embarrassment.
He went and sat behind the upper room
of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
He laid it out, recited and repeated it, recited and repeated it.
phrases.notes: The 'it' is מסכת עוקצין, the one they planned to test him on.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁמְעִינְהוּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בֶּן קֻדְשַׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Response to the plan made in Step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יעקב בן קדשי protects the נשיא's honor by quietly reviewing עוקצין where he can hear.

steps.title: The נשיא notices and prepares
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל hears the review, suspects something is being planned in the בית מדרש, and learns עוקצין carefully.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: What is this happening in front of us? Perhaps, Heaven forbid, something is going on in the בית מדרש. He focused his mind and learned it.
steps.whatsHappening: The נשיא picks up the hint, guesses there is a plan against him, and learns the מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quiet hint from Step 21 works. The נשיא understands that the review is a warning, so he takes it seriously and gets ready.

phrases.english: He said: What is this happening in front of us?
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, hearing the review from behind his room.

phrases.english: Perhaps, Heaven forbid,
there is something going on in the study hall.
He focused his mind and learned it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: מַאי דְּקַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Result of the review in Step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נשיא understands the warning and learns עוקצין.

steps.title: The test fails and the נשיא passes
steps.stepSummary: The next day they ask him to teach עוקצין. He teaches it fully, then tells them that if he had not learned it, they would have embarrassed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day they said to him: Let the master come and teach us עוקצין. He began and taught it. After he finished, he said to them: If I had not learned it, you would have embarrassed me.
steps.whatsHappening: The plan from Step 20 is carried out, but it fails because the נשיא is ready. He lets them know he saw through it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words 'you would have embarrassed me' show he now knows the request was a trap and not an honest question. This sets up the punishment in the next step.

phrases.english: The next day they said to him:
Let the master come and teach us עוקצין.
He began and taught.
After he finished,
he said to them: If I had not learned it,
you would have embarrassed me.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִמְחַר אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The plan of Step 20 is tried and fails because of the preparation in Step 22
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נשיא passes the test and shows that he knew it was meant to embarrass him.

steps.title: Sent out, but still sending in Torah
steps.stepSummary: The נשיא has רבי מאיר and רבי נתן put out of the בית מדרש. From outside they throw in notes with questions, and they also send answers to the questions nobody inside could answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gave an order and they were put out of the בית מדרש. They would write questions on notes and throw them inside. Questions that were answered were answered. For the ones that were not answered, they wrote the answers and threw those in too.
steps.whatsHappening: The punishment is given: the two scholars are sent out. Even from outside, they keep adding to the learning inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars inside could not answer some of the questions, but רבי מאיר and רבי נתן could. This shows that the בית מדרש needed their Torah, and it leads straight into רבי יוסי's protest.

keyTerms.meaning: A note, a slip of paper

phrases.english: He gave an order, and they put them out of the study hall.
They would write difficult questions on a note
and throw them in there.
Those that were answered were answered;
those that were not answered,
they wrote answers and threw them in.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּקֵּיד וְאַפְּקִינְהוּ מִבֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The punishment that follows the failed plan in Step 23
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר and רבי נתן are sent out, but they keep giving Torah to the בית מדרש through notes.

steps.title: רבי יוסי protests: the Torah is outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי complains to the other scholars that the Torah, meaning these great scholars, is outside while they themselves sit inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to them: The Torah is outside, and we are inside?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי makes a sharp protest against keeping רבי מאיר and רבי נתן out of the בית מדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His question is not really asking for information. It is a protest that it makes no sense to shut out the people who are answering the questions nobody else can answer. It pushes for bringing them back.
steps.whatToRemember: The plan to embarrass the נשיא failed and led to the two scholars being sent out. Their Torah was still so needed that רבי יוסי protested having them outside.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to them:
The Torah is outside, and we are inside?
phrases.notes: By 'Torah' he means רבי מאיר and רבי נתן, whose answers were coming in from outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: תּוֹרָה מִבַּחוּץ וְאָנוּ מִבִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Protest against the result described in Step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי protests that the Torah scholars are kept outside while the others sit inside.

steps.title: The נשיא lets them back in, but with a penalty
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees to let רבי מאיר and רבי נתן back into the בית מדרש. As a penalty, their teachings will not be said in their names.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said to the scholars: Let us bring them back in. But we will penalize them by not saying teachings in their names.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבי יוסי's complaint, the נשיא agrees to bring the two scholars back. He sets a penalty: their names will be left off their teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars inside now see that the Torah of these two is too important to lose, so they are let back in. The punishment does not touch their learning, which stays in the בית מדרש. It only takes away the honor of having their names on it, which fits what they tried to do: take away the נשיא's honor.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said to them:
Let us bring them in,
but we will penalize them
that we will not say a teaching in their names.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: נִיעַיְּילִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's complaint by bringing the scholars back in, but with a penalty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two scholars may come back in, but their teachings will be quoted without their names.

steps.title: How their teachings were quoted without their names
steps.stepSummary: From then on, רבי מאיר's teachings were quoted as 'אחרים' (others) and רבי נתן's as 'יש אומרים' (some say).
steps.simpleTranslation: They quoted רבי מאיר as 'אחרים' (others), and רבי נתן as 'יש אומרים' (some say).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how the penalty worked in practice. Each scholar got a nameless label in place of his own name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains where two nameless labels come from. In these cases, 'אחרים' stood for רבי מאיר and 'יש אומרים' stood for רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: They called or labeled (literally, they brought up)
'Others', the label used for רבי מאיר
'Some say', the label used for רבי נתן

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the origin of the labels 'אחרים' for רבי מאיר and 'יש אומרים' for רבי נתן, and the next step shows the 'אחרים' label still being used a generation later.

phrases.english: They called Rabbi Meir 'Others,'
and Rabbi Natan 'Some say.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַסִּיקוּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the penalty from step 26 was carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר is quoted as 'אחרים' and רבי נתן as 'יש אומרים'.

steps.title: A dream tells them to make peace, but only one goes
steps.stepSummary: Both scholars are told in a dream to go and make peace with the נשיא. רבי נתן goes. רבי מאיר does not, because he says dreams do not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were shown in their dreams: Go, make peace with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבי נתן went. רבי מאיר did not go. He said: Dreams make no difference, neither for good nor for bad.
steps.whatsHappening: Both scholars get the same message in a dream: go and make up with the נשיא. Each reacts differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן takes the dream seriously and goes. רבי מאיר holds the principle that dreams carry no weight, so he does not feel bound by it. This sets up the next step, where we see how the נשיא treats רבי נתן when he arrives.

keyTerms.meaning: Make peace with him, appease him

keyTerms.term: דִּבְרֵי חֲלוֹמוֹת לֹא מַעֲלִין וְלֹא מוֹרִידִין
keyTerms.meaning: Dreams make no difference (literally, they neither raise up nor bring down)

phrases.english: They were shown in their dreams:
Go, appease Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
Rabbi Natan went,
Rabbi Meir did not go,
he said: Matters of dreams
do not raise up and do not bring down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחְווֹ לְהוּ בְּחֶלְמַיְיהוּ: זִילוּ פַּיְּיסוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story forward: after the penalty, a dream pushes the two scholars to make peace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר holds that dreams have no binding weight. רבי נתן acts on the dream.

steps.title: The נשיא's sharp words to רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: When רבי נתן comes, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells him: your father's importance may have made you אב בית דין, but will it make you נשיא too?
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי נתן went, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said to him: Fine, your father's fancy belt helped you become אב בית דין. Will we also make you נשיא?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן comes to make peace. The נשיא answers with a sharp remark about his attempt to take over the role of נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'belt' stands for the high status of רבי נתן's father. The נשיא admits that this status helped רבי נתן get the second-highest post, אב בית דין. He makes clear it will not carry him to the top post of נשיא, which is the post the plan in step 20 meant to give him.

keyTerms.meaning: A belt, here a sign of status
Head of the court, second to the נשיא

steps.whatToRemember: The נשיא's honor is upheld. Family status can bring someone far, but it does not entitle him to the top post. The next step jumps a generation ahead to show the 'אחרים' label still in use.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Natan went,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said to him:
Granted that your father's belt helped you
phrases.notes: The belt was a fancy piece of clothing worn by important people. Here it stands for his father's high status.

phrases.english: to become head of the court,
shall we also make you נשיא?!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲזַל רַבִּי נָתָן, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened when רבי נתן followed the dream and came to make peace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Status from one's father earned רבי נתן the post of אב בית דין, but not the post of נשיא.

steps.title: A generation later: רבי teaches his son a teaching of 'אחרים'
steps.stepSummary: The story jumps ahead. רבי teaches his son רבן שמעון a teaching that begins 'אחרים אומרים: if it were a substitute'. This sets up the next exchange.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי was teaching his son רבן שמעון: 'אחרים say: If it were a substitute...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves forward to the next generation. It begins quoting a teaching labeled 'אחרים', and this sets up the next step, which continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we see the penalty from step 27 still in force years later. רבי מאיר's teaching is being taught as 'אחרים'. The quote stops in the middle, so the rest of the teaching and the son's reaction come next.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute, an animal swapped for a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people named רבן שמעון. The רבן שמעון here is רבי's son, the grandson of the נשיא from the story.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi was teaching Rabban Shimon his son,
'Others say:'
phrases.notes: Remember from step 27 that 'Others' means רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: 'If it were a substitute'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרֵיהּ, אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Jumps a generation ahead to show the 'אחרים' label still being used, and sets up the next exchange.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי teaches his son a teaching of רבי מאיר under the label 'אחרים'.
